_comment: Screenshot design spec, read by `ship shots capture|render|verify`. caption-band mode: the finished 1242x2688 composites Apple already serves are the base, and only the caption band is repainted per locale. Geometry is committed rather than re-derived because Figma's render endpoint is quota-limited on the starter plan.

source._frameIdsNote: Only frame 1's node id survived the original extraction. `ship shots figma --export <ids>` needs explicit ids for the rest; the drift check does not, since it reads the file version.
source.note: Cached from the Figma REST node tree. /v1/images 429s after a handful of calls on the starter plan, so the mockup pixels cannot be re-exported on demand — which is why this app repaints Apple's composites instead of rebuilding them.

base._note: Downloaded by `ship shots capture` from the public App Store lookup endpoint — the live English composites, at the spec canvas size.

fonts._note: Cambay covers Latin and Devanagari only, so ja/ko fall back to Noto Sans. Both Noto files are variable: without the explicit wght they open on Regular and every CJK caption renders lighter and narrower than the design.

type._note: Greedy, not balanced, and inside each frame's own Figma box width — because that is what Figma does. A balanced wrap reads better in isolation but breaks lines where the designer did not: it split frame 2 as 'Log a service / in 15 seconds.' where Figma had 'Log a service in 15 / seconds.'

band._note: The licence for this mode: in all six frames the caption sits on flat background, separated from the mockup — ~94% one solid colour, the remaining 6% being the caption glyphs. flatMin turns that property into a gate, so a redesign that puts artwork in the band fails the render instead of destroying it.

_framesNote: Six frames, in App Store order. Frames 1-4 are the August 2026 re-authored art; frames 5-6 (ScreenShotAppStore4 = onboarding step 1/5, ScreenShotAppStore5 = onboarding step 4/5 summary) were re-authored on the same art later and appended, which is why their keys again sit out of z-order. The base composites were re-authored outside Figma, so the frame keys no longer track the old Figma z-order: the array order is the shipped order and each key is kept only because 16 locales of calibrated caption copy hang off it. Key to what the art shows: ScreenShotAppStore3 = vehicle detail with an overdue oil change, ScreenShotAppStore6 = the garage list, ScreenShotAppStore1 = full service history, ScreenShotAppStore2 = the log sheet. mockTop/mockH are measured off the art; every caption sits above the mockup, where frame 2 previously carried it below. The near-black band background was snapped to #000000 in the raw art on frames 1-4, because upscaling left per-pixel noise that dropped band flatness under the 0.85 gate on every frame; frames 5-6 arrive already flat at #454A50.
